turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: Hey Maya. I'm ready to put on my hiring manager hat for our mock screen whenever you are. Should we jump right in?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Hey Wren. Yeah, let's do it, I've got my glass of water ready and I'm as set as I'll ever be.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: Stepping into character now. Thanks for jumping on today, Maya. Could you start by telling me a little about yourself?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Sure, well, um, I actually started out thinking I'd do pure data analysis, but during my program I realized I enjoyed talking with people way more. So I took classes in communications and project management, and I worked on group projects where I had to coordinate across different teams, and then I got involved in student associations where we planned events and handled outreach, which made me realize I really want to be customer-facing and talk to prospects every day.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: Got it. Outbound roles take a lot of grit, so could you tell me about a time you did cold outreach to hit a target?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Definitely. When we organized our student career fair, we suddenly had a sponsor drop out right before the event, so I picked up the phone and cold-called forty alumni in just one week. Most were surprised to hear from a student out of nowhere, but I ended up landing three sponsors to fill the gap.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: That wraps up our quick screen, and I'm stepping out of interviewer mode now. How did that feel from your side?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Whew, glad that's done. Honestly, my opening felt pretty messy, but how did it sound to you?

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: Your alumni story was crisp, but your answer on tell me about yourself rambled and ran past two minutes. Did you notice where it got tangled?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yeah, I totally rambled through tell me about yourself and went way over two minutes before I even mentioned sales. I got stuck listing courses instead of focusing on what's relevant.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: That happens easily when you trace the whole timeline. What if you anchor it on where you are today and why you want tech sales?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That makes total sense. I want to write out a couple bullet points for that structure so I don't wander off next time.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: Writing bullet points instead of a script will keep it sounding natural. How are your nerves holding up after doing that run?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: A lot better now, actually. Getting the first clunky practice run out of the way always takes the edge off.
